proxy_language: Classical Nahuatl (Aztec/Mexica of Tenochtitlan, c. 1428-1521 CE)
proxy_rationale: The 'Fifth Sun' (Nahui Ollin, Ollin Tonatiuh) is the Mexica cosmological era; the court of Tenochtitlan spoke Classical Nahuatl, which is richly attested in Colonial-era alphabetic texts (Florentine Codex, Cantares Mexicanos, Bancroft Dialogues) and dictionaries (Molina 1571). Names can be built directly in attested Nahuatl.
phonology: Consonants: p t k kw (spelled c/qu, cu/uc) ; ts (tz) tl (affricate, spelled tl) ch (tS) ; s (c/z) sh (x) ; m n ; l ; w (hu/uh) ; y ; glottal stop (saltillo, written h or ' in some editions). No b d g f r. Vowels: a e i o, with contrastive length (long macron: ā ē ī ō). Stress penultimate (so no stress marking in names).
phonotactics: Syllables (C)V(V:)(C). Onsets are single consonants (tl, tz, ch, qu, cu count as single units). No onset clusters. Codas: single consonant or glottal stop (h); word-final tl/tli/tin/in are absolutive suffixes. Final consonants in words are typically -l, -n, -tl, -h, -c, -z, -x. No vowel-initial restrictions (words can start with a vowel). Hiatus occurs (e.g. cuauh-, tlā-oh-). Penultimate stress is predictable, so no accents are written in standard orthography.
orthography: Classical (Carochi/Andrews) orthography in Latin script: c (before a,o)/qu (before e,i) = /k/; cu/uc = /kw/; z (before a,o) / c (before e,i) = /s/; tz = /ts/; tl = /tɬ/; ch; x = /ʃ/; hu/uh = /w/; y; h = glottal stop or aspiration; macrons optional for long vowels (can be dropped). No letters b, d, f, g, j, k, r, v in native words. Final -tl, -tli, -li, -in are absolutive suffixes of nouns.
morphology: Polysynthetic-leaning, agglutinative; head-final in nominal compounds. Nouns: absolutive suffixes (-tl, -tli, -li, -in; or -0 after consonant stems in a few cases), plural -meh / -tin / reduplication in animates. Possessed nouns lose absolutive and take possessive prefixes (no- my, mo- your, i- his/her, to- our, in/im- their) plus -uh/-huh or -0 suffixes. Verbs: obligatory subject prefix (ni- I, ti- you/we, 0- he/she), object prefixes (k-/qui-, tē- someone, tla- something), tense suffixes, directionals (-ti-, -ko). Reduplication marks plurals and diminutives (e.g. tlācatl -> tlahtlācah). Locative suffixes: -c, -co, -tlan, -tla, -pan, -nahuac, -tzinco. Diminutive/honorific -tzin (reverential, essential on court titles). Agentive nouns: tla-...-ni or -qui, -ni (e.g. tlaquimilolli). Adjectival nouns: -tic, -ac. Relational nouns: -tech, -nahuac, -pan, -tlan.
compounding: Compound nouns are head-final: modifier + head with the modifier stripped of its absolutive suffix (atl + tepetl -> altepetl 'city (water-hill)'). 'X of Y' names are formed either by (a) compounding Y-X (xōchi-cihuātl 'flower woman'), or by (b) possessive construction: possessor + possessed with possessive prefix i- (Tōnatiuh itēcpan?), or (c) locative suffixes: Y-tlan 'place of Y', Y-co 'in/at Y', Y-pan 'on Y', Y-tlān 'near/among Y'. Place names: Y-tlan / Y-co / Y-pan / Y-tepēc 'at the hill of Y'. Occupational names: tla- + object + -ni (maker). Divine names: noun + adjective compounds (Huītzilōpōchtli = hummingbird + left; Tezcatlipoca = smoking mirror; Quetzalcōātl = quetzal-feather serpent).
noun_phrase_order: Modifier before head (adjective/modifier + noun: yancuic calli 'new house'; possessor before possessed: nicān mo-tlaxcal 'here is your tortilla'). Genitive constructions are possessor-possessed: tlahtoāni icalli 'the ruler's house'. Numerals precede nouns. Relational nouns follow the noun they govern (tēpan 'on the hill' = tepētl-pan).

notes: No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word unless the language is Goidelic; Nahuatl is not Goidelic, so avoid any Goidelic lookalikes. Avoid b d f g j k r v in native-style names (the current game strings Tiyeh, Viqote, Nihyaza violate this: v, q without u, and non-Nahuatl shapes). Use the absolutive suffix -tl/-tli/-li/-in only when the word stands alone; strip it inside compounds. Use -tzin for reverential/court titles (tlahtoani -> Tlatoani, Motecuhzoma Xocoyotzin). Nahuatl spelling of 'cu' = /kw/, 'qu' = /k/ before e/i. Avoid inventing Spanish-sounding endings.
